t.1.31.1: Śaunaka said: O son of a sūta, you have told the reason for the curse laid upon the serpents by their mother, and upon Vinatā by her son.
t.1.31.3: But you do not recite the names of the serpents, O son of a Sūta. We wish to hear their names, at least those of the foremost among them.
t.1.31.2: You have told of the granting of boons by their husband to Kadrū and Vinatā, and likewise you have told the names of the two birds, the sons of Vinatā.
t.1.31.4: Because of their great number, O ascetic rich in penance, I shall not recite the names of all the serpents; but hear from me the names of the foremost among them.
t.1.31.5: Śeṣa was born first, and Vāsuki immediately after him; then Airāvata and Takṣaka, and Karkoṭaka and Dhanaṃjaya.
t.1.31.6: Kāliya and Maṇināga, and the Nāga Āpūraṇa as well, and likewise the Nāga Piñjaraka, Elāpattra, and then Vāmana.
t.1.31.7: Likewise the two Nāgas Nīla and Ānīla, and likewise Kalmāṣa and Śabala, Āryaka and Ādika, and the Nāga Śalapotaka.
t.1.31.8: Sumanomukha, Dadhimukha, and likewise Vimalapiṇḍaka, Āpta and Koṭanaka too, Śaṅkha, and likewise Vālaśikha.
t.1.31.9: Niṣṭhyūnaka, Hemaguha, Nahuṣa, and Piṅgala as well; Bāhyakarṇa, Hastipada, and likewise Mudgarapiṇḍaka.
t.1.31.10: Kambala and Aśvatara too, and likewise the serpent Kālīyaka; the two serpents Vṛtta and Saṃvartaka, and the two known as the Padmas.
t.1.31.11: The Nāga Śaṅkhanaka, and likewise another, Sphaṇḍaka; Kṣemaka, the great Nāga, and likewise the Nāga Piṇḍāraka.
t.1.31.12: Karavīra, Puṣpadaṃṣṭra, Eḍaka, Bilvapāṇḍuka, Mūṣakāda, Śaṅkhaśiras, Pūrṇadaṃṣṭra, and Haridraka.
t.1.31.13: Aparājita and Jyotika, and likewise the serpent Śrīvaha; Kauravya and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Puṣkara and likewise Śalyaka.
t.1.31.14: Virajas and Subāhu and the mighty Śālipiṇḍa, Hastibhadra, Piṭharaka, Mukhara, and Koṇavāsana.
t.1.31.16: These Nāgas have been named according to their eminence, O best of the twice-born; because of the multitude of their names, the others have not been mentioned.
t.1.31.15: Kuñjara and Kurara, and likewise the serpent Prabhākara; Kumuda and Kumudākṣa, Tittiri and likewise Halika; Karkara and Akarkara, both of them, and Kuṇḍodara and Mahodara.
t.1.31.17: The offspring of these, and the lineage of that offspring, are beyond counting; thinking so, I do not name them, O best of the twice-born.
t.1.31.18: Many thousands, millions and hundreds of millions of serpents are here, O ascetic rich in austerities, truly impossible to count.
